text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

As the Kennett Government's review of the Victorian Audit Act closes to submissions on January 20, it has been revealed that the latest performance audits being conducted by the Victorian Auditor-General's Office include some of the Victorian Premier's pet projects - the Melbourne Exhibition Centre, the Sports and Aquatic Centre in Albert Park, the State Library redevelopment and the refurbishment of the Regent Theatre. Page 2.

Federal Liberal backbencher Lou Liebermann said yesterday the Federal Government could pass oil-industry specific amendments to the Trade Practices Act if oil companies were unable to prove they did not unfairly raise petrol prices over the Christmas holiay period. Page 4.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics' annual trade union membership census, released on Friday, showed the first signs that the long-term decline in Australian unionisation rates may be bottoming out at around a third of the workforce. Financial union memership figures of 35 per cent were the first figures since 1991 that have not shown a decline. Page 5.

A spokesman for Federal Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith has dismissed a warning by the Community and Public Sector Union that employees should not sign new individual or collective employment agreements without expert advice, saying the warning's misleading and gratuitous. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In what could be one of Australia's biggest defence export deals, Melbourne-based company Transfield Defence Systems looks set to gain around A$2.5 billion of a multi-billion dollar program to overhaul The Philippines' navy. The company's chances of winnng the project have been boosted by the Federal Government's in-principle agreement to provide a loan to The Philippines to buy two search and rescue vessels to be built by Transfield in Western Australia. Page 1.

Award-winning Australian novelist Elizabeth Jolley lost her second home in the fire storm that engulfed Western Australia's Avon Valley over the weekend, yet as she inspected the ruins of her Wooroloo cottage she counted herself lucky that no-one lost a life. Jolley's home was one of 12 destroyed in the fires. Page 1.

As millions of dollars of prizemoney comes under threat and jockeys face fines for not riding over the weekend as part of a national strike over jockey pay demands, the Gold Coast Turf Club will ask the Queensland Government to ensure the running of next aturday's A$1 million Honda Magic Millions Classic. A Gold Coast meeting was one of four cancelled on Saturday as a result of the strike. Page 1.

A survey by the University of New South Wales psychology unit claims over 50 per cent of doctors and nurses have cried over the death of a patient, or the emotional reaction of the patient's family. As some claim they have been ridiculed for crying by thir colleagues, the Australian Medical Association admits this is a culture that frowns upon the display of emotions. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Talks will be conducted this week between the Sydney Organising Committee for the Olympic Games and the International Olympic Committee over the possible hosting of a full-scale world Youth Games in 1999. The proposal was supported on the weekend by IOC resident Juan Antonio Samaranch and would be used as an official Olympic test event if approved. Page 1.

With New South Wales school students receiving their Higher School Certificate results tomorrow, they will be happy to hear State universities will be forced to drop their entry requirements in 1997 because of a decline in the numbers of students applyingfor university places. However, the bad news for those students applying for university is that they will have to pay more for their degrees, following Federal Government Higher Education Contribution Scheme increases. Page 1.

Tim Fischer, acting as Prime Minister for 19 days while John Howard holidays with his family at Hawks Nest, began his term at his family farm at Boree Creek, near Wagga Wagga in New South Wales, and spent this weekend at his flat in Sydney's Bronte. Fischer's holiday office is becoming as well known as that taken by Doug Anthony in the caravan next to his beach house on the State's north coast. Page 1.

Australian researchers are looking at a drug developed by Spanish drug rehabilitation expert Dr Juan Jose Legarda that treats heroin addiction. The treatment, ultra-rapid opiate detoxification, gives addicts doses of naltrexone every 45 minutes for six hours while they are under general anaesthetic, which replaces heroin in the brain and prevents drug-induced euphoria. Page 3.
THE AGE

The Victorian Government is investigating the alleged downgrading by five public hospitals - the Royal Melbourne, Royal Women's, Mornington Peninsula, Geelong, and Angliss hospitals - of about 1000 patients in an attempt to obtain more funding by switched patients from semi-urgent to non-urgent waiting lists. Page A1.

National Farmers Federation president Donald McGauchie said yesterday farmers would not negotiate with Aboriginal Australians over native title rights on pastoral leases, saying agreements between farmers and Aborigines were not legally binding and would not resolve the land ownership questions raised by the High Court's Wik native title judgement. Page A1.

A biennial survey by The Age of 28 economists from business, academia and the financial sector has suggested recent cuts have not been enough to lift the hopes of Australia's leading forecasters, who see growth continuing to slide and unemployment improving little. Page A1.

The arrival of the world's best woman tennis player, Steffi Graf, in Melbourne signals the start of the city's tennis season, with the Australian Open beginning next Monday. The Open, which last year was watched by 390,000 people, offers prizemoney of A$.5 million and will see many stars return, including Graf, Pete Sampras, Monica Seles, and Mary Pierce. Page A1.
